title: Half Ice Finnish Series Setup
description: A flexible half-ice skills setup built around multiple tire lanes so coaches can run repeated skating and puck-control variations such as mohawk pivots, backward underhandling, escape turns, and long reaches.
coaching_points: Open the hips fully on mohawk pivots and keep the feet active.
Use smooth, quiet touches while underhandling the puck backward.
On escape turns, protect the puck and rotate away from the obstacle.
Use long reaches outside the tires while keeping the head up.

title: 2 v 1 Net Play Drills for Defensemen
description: A three-location 2-on-1 net-play progression that starts behind the net or in either corner. Two forwards attack from below the goal line while one defender protects the front of the net and manages passing lanes.
coaching_points: Defender keeps the stick on the ice and tracks both forwards.
Stay in a strong stance and protect the middle of the net-front area.
Forward without the puck finds open ice around the crease.
Puck carrier attacks the front of the net and uses the support option when available.

title: DZ Corner Battle 1 v 2 to 2 v 3
description: A defensive-zone corner battle progression that begins 1-on-2 and builds to 2-on-3. Defenders learn pressure-and-support responsibilities while offensive players work to protect the puck and create a scoring chance.
coaching_points: First defender pressures the puck while the next defender reads and supports.
If pressure is beaten, the support defender takes over and the first defender recovers underneath.
Offensive players protect the puck and use support when the progression becomes 2-on-3.
Defenders communicate before switching pressure and support roles.

title: Pass Through 2 Players out of the Corner
description: A corner passing progression where the first player curls back, moves the puck to the next player in line, then jumps into the slot between two defenders to receive a lead pass and shoot.
coaching_points: Jump hard into open ice between the two defenders.
Keep the stick on the ice and present a clear target.
Lead the shooter with the return pass rather than passing behind them.
Progress from passive sticks to active defender sticks as execution improves.

title: D-Zone Coverage Tire Drill
description: A two-part 5-on-5 defensive-zone coverage drill. Teams first play live in-zone; on the next whistle the three defending forwards leave around neutral-zone tires, then race back into the zone and reestablish coverage.
coaching_points: Defenders keep sticks in lanes and force the puck toward the outside.
Communicate continuously while sorting coverage on the return.
Forwards sprint back into structure rather than drifting into assignments.
Offensive players use the temporary numerical advantage to move into open passing lanes.

title: Outlet Game
description: A cross-ice 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 game where each team must use an outlet before it can attack. Outlets can move along the goal line or blue line and may be used repeatedly during a possession.
coaching_points: Transition quickly after possession changes.
Pass to an outlet and immediately jump into open space.
Use give-and-go plays to create separation.
Defenders keep sticks in lanes and angle attackers outside.

title: 3 on 2 Keep Away Game
description: A confined 3-on-2 keep-away game around the faceoff circle. Three offensive players work the perimeter while two defenders protect the middle, block lanes, and try to create a turnover.
coaching_points: Defenders keep sticks on the ice and recover toward the middle after pressure.
Offensive players show targets and use crisp passes around the perimeter.
Use fakes and deception to open passing lanes.
Make area passes when a direct tape-to-tape lane is not available.

title: 4 vs 2 Transition Game
description: A continuous 4-on-2 possession and transition game. When the two defenders win the puck, two teammates enter as outlets and the former offensive team leaves two players behind to become the next defenders.
coaching_points: Players waiting on the blue line stay alert for the transition.
Defenders use active sticks, protect the middle, and angle attackers outside.
New offensive players recognize available teammates immediately after the turnover.
Offensive players without the puck move constantly into support space.

title: Weak Side Attack
description: A two-part rush drill that starts with a 2-on-1, then activates a second puck and turns into a 3-on-2. The new puck carrier attacks the weak side to create time for teammates to join the rush.
coaching_points: Puck carrier attacks the weak side and scans for support.
Defenders protect the middle with sticks in passing lanes.
Forwards communicate while filling lanes on the 3-on-2.
Use the weak-side route to delay just enough for support to arrive.

title: Puck In Skates Skill Builder
description: A puck-control skill builder that gives players repeated touches controlling pucks in and around their skates, then moving the puck quickly back to the stick.
coaching_points: Practice using both the front and back skate to control the puck.
Move the puck from the skates back to the stick quickly.
Keep the upper body calm while the feet make the correction.
Repeat on both sides to build comfort handling imperfect passes.
